rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
prompt: ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Quehuoque, the pure black swallow-shaped fire-dispersing bird. ANATOMY: one pure-black swallow-sized bird, one head, two black natural eyes, two swept pointed wings, two feet and one forked swallow tail, all feathers unburnt. MOMENT: Sweep straight toward camera through the center of a flame, spread black wings filling frame while the flames bend and retreat forcefully away on both sides. POWER: Fire disperses by itself around the bird leaving a dramatic clean dark gap; the bird extinguishes fire, it does NOT emit fire and its eyes do not glow. SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle; subject fills frame, natural documented size, never unsupported gigantic. LIGHT & WEATHER: one warm lateral source, deep shadows, crisp rim, physically moving dust/water only. SURFACE: tactile coarse textures, rich walnut/antique-gold palette. SETTING: an imperial Chinese sleeping hall suggested in deep shadow, a human-held wax candle below as natural-size comparison; select Duyang Zabian variant. MOOD: dangerous or awe-inspiring, never ordinary, cute, calm or decorative. HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, symbols, logos, border, signature, watermark; no extra heads or limbs; no franchises; no nudity, transparent clothes, blood, wounds or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon lines or energy ribbons.
